The emulator's Android Keystore is software-backed, so the key protection of the stored tokens is not hardware-backed there.
Re-consent asks for the OTP again: eSignet Go keeps no browser session. Health Card's explainer screen says so.
The server's runtime store is in memory, so an eSignet restart ends every Hub session; the e2e suite uses this to test the ended session.

Revoking the device secret (rule R27, Hub "Sign out of all apps") ends its session record, but access tokens already issued to Health Card stay valid until they expire: eSignet keeps the token deny list off. Without network the record ends by its time to live; the deleted DPoP key already blocks every use.

The GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on GitHub for pushes to main, but this machine has no GitHub CLI or API access to the runs, so no hosted run result is recorded. Every job was replayed on Linux containers instead (row CI-LINUX).

Emulator tests run on one emulator image (AVD ps03_api34, Google APIs x86_64, API 34, Chrome 113), not on other Android versions or browsers. The browser login steps of the UI tests can time out on a busy machine; a rerun passes.

The upstream Postman folders need the Postman desktop app (they use WebCrypto and top-level await that newman 6.2.2 lacks); nobody on the team has run them there. The Native SSO folder runs under newman.
No TalkBack or accessibility scanner run exists; accessibility is covered by JVM screen tests of both apps at 200 % font (HubScreensTest, CardScreensTest) and by the design rules only.
Nothing was run on a physical phone or on Linux or macOS machines of the team; the Go tests run in a Linux container on a Windows 11 laptop, and the CI jobs were replayed in Linux containers there.
